html:
The siege of Kansala, capital of Kaabu, in 1867, by the Fula armies of the Imamate of Futa Jallon.

After a long siege, tradition says the last mansa, Janke Waali, set fire to his gunpowder store rather than surrender, killing defenders and many attackers. The fall ended the Mandinka kingdom that had ruled the region for centuries, and the Fula took over its eastern lands, which they held until Portuguese conquest. It is part of the series of Fula jihads that remade West Africa from the 18th century. The story is sung by griots in the Gambia, Senegal and Guinea-Bissau. See also the Mande peoples.
